paper_title: Can LLMs Solve longer Math Word Problems Better
caption: (left) and (right) of scaling up SFT dataset across various model scales in the LLaMA-2 family. The results suggest scaling up model scales and SFT dataset can further improve .
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effect of scaling up model scales and Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) datasets on the performance of LLaMA-2 models, specifically measuring the CoLeG-R percentage. The horizontal axis lists three model variants: LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-2-70B. The vertical axis represents the CoLeG-R percentage, labeled with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 80, marked with intervals of 10. The chart features four groups of bars, each representing a different SFT configuration: no SFT (blue), + SFT on D0 (yellow), + SFT on D0, D1 (purple), and + SFT on D0, D1, D2 (red). For each model variant, the bars are arranged in ascending order of SFT configurations. The approximate CoLeG-R percentages for the shortest and tallest bars are 65% for LLaMA-2-7B with no SFT and 87% for LLaMA-2-13B and LLaMA-2-70B with + SFT on D0, D1, D2. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or outlining, and no specific sorting beyond the SFT configurations is applied.
